analysis.title: View From The Knowledge Network
key_insights: Multiple investor types cut risk. Hedge funds had their third largest de-gross YTD, with net exposure now in the 10th percentile on a 5y lookback. Composite positioning moved further underweight, driven by large reductions from Balanced and Value funds.

Risk Control funds sold an estimated $160bn of equities over two days, cutting exposure to the 65th percentile from the 93rd percentile last week. CTAs are in the 9th percentile. Levered and inverse ETFs sold $30bn of equity risk on Friday's move and are now below median exposure.

Index and single-name implied volatility repriced higher over the past few days. VIX and VIXEQ both closed at their highest levels since July. Skew also rose sharply, which suggests clients hedged quickly.
After a second day of heavy systematic selling, the UBS model estimates Risk Control turns to buyers on Tuesday. CTA selling is largely complete with limited incremental impact from here.

Monday systematic selling was estimated at about $85-115bn: Risk Control $65-85bn, CTA $10-15bn, Leveraged ETFs $10-15bn. Selling was concentrated in Nasdaq, with -$16bn excess flow to sell in the S&P 500 versus -$53bn in the Nasdaq.

Real money support was strong over the last 3 down days. UBS RMM clients bought the dip on all 3 days, foreign-listed US ETFs bought all 3 days, and Multi-Asset Managers and Risk Parity bought on Monday, with equity/bond correlation back to negative.

UBS (Karl Keirstead) defends PLTR after the print. Revenue growth was 96% in 3Q, and guidance with a normal beat implies about 100% growth in 4Q, which does not point to slowing demand. Sequentially flat RPO was driven by a decision to ramp sovereign AI customers quickly, which shifts the mix to contracts under 12 months that do not appear in RPO.

UBS (David Vogt) stays Neutral on AAPL after the September-quarter print. Hardware (iPhone and Mac) was a bit better than expected, but guidance points to growth concerns: growth is becoming more ASP/price-driven, services are slowing, and gross margin is under pressure from higher memory costs and the Siri ramp, with valuation elevated at about 36x NTM.

market_movers.rationale: Keirstead says high-90s revenue growth and 60%+ margins make the shares compelling at 49x CY27E FCF. The flat RPO pushback reflects a mix shift to contracts under 12 months.
Vogt sees growth concerns in guidance: more ASP-driven growth, slowing services, and gross margin pressure from memory costs and the Siri ramp, at about 36x NTM valuation.

earnings_insights: PLTR 3Q reported revenue growth of 96% y/y. Guidance, assuming a normal beat, implies about 100% growth in 4Q (UBS view). RPO was sequentially flat, attributed to a mix shift toward contracts under 12 months from sovereign AI customers.

AAPL September-quarter (fiscal Q3 per report) print was a bit better than expected on hardware (iPhone and Mac). Dec-quarter services growth guidance is 8-9% versus UBS's prior expectation of 11.6%. Dec-quarter gross margin guidance is 45-46%, which UBS attributes to higher memory costs and the Siri ramp.
risk_factors: PLTR: sequentially flat RPO is the key pushback on the print.
AAPL: slowing services growth, gross margin pressure from memory costs and Siri ramp, and elevated valuation.
vol_and_positioning: Hedge fund net exposure is in the 10th percentile on a 5y lookback after the third largest de-gross YTD.
CTAs are in the 9th percentile of positioning. Risk Control exposure fell to the 65th percentile from the 93rd percentile last week.
Levered and inverse ETFs sold $30bn of equity risk on Friday, and exposure is now below median.
VIX and VIXEQ closed at their highest levels since July. Skew rose sharply as hedge costs increased.
Estimated systematic flows: Monday selling of $85-115bn. Tuesday Risk Control buying of $10-15bn, with CTA and Leveraged ETF rebalancing dependent on market moves.
Eq/Bond correlation is back to negative.
